advisory.finding: The MCP `bridge_check_access` tool is registered unconditionally as a read tool (not behind the readonly or allow_jira_sync gates), but the underlying access check creates, labels, property-writes, and deletes a live Jira issue. advisory.finding: bridge_check_access is registered as a READ_ONLY_OPEN_WORLD MCP tool available under REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1 and without REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC, yet it creates, labels, writes an issue property on, and deletes a real Jira issue — so a server the operator has set to read-only can still be driven to mutate the external Jira system, contradicting the documented policy that REBAR_MCP_READONLY blocks every mutation.
scenarios: An operator runs the MCP server with REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1 expecting no external side effects; an MCP client calls bridge_check_access and causes issue creation/deletion in the configured Jira project.
An untrusted/low-trust MCP client triggers repeated external Jira create/delete churn against the DIG project via a tool advertised as readOnlyHint=True.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Route `bridge_sync` through the same pause-gate + pass-lock/heartbeat/in-flight acquisition as `main()`, or make `run_pass_result` for the sync route acquire and hold the reconciler lock and honor the durable pause.
evidence: src/rebar/_lib_ops.py:165 `orchestrator = _engine_module("rebar_reconciler.__main__")` then `result = orchestrator.run_pass_result(... route=route)` for route 'sync'

run_pass_result at src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:455-520 loads `_advisory` only for `lock_lost_cls` and calls `reconcile.reconcile_once` directly — no `acquire_pass_lock`, no `_Heartbeat`, no `_pause_exit_code`

Pause/lock/steal/phase-gate all live in `main()`: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:632 `pause_exit = _pause_exit_code(...)`, :654 `_post_pause_preflight`, :693 `_acquire_or_adopt_pass_lock`, :698 `_Heartbeat(...)`
reconcile_once does no pause/lock: search of reconcile.py for 'pause' returns no matches; src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py:143-204 only fetch/diff/apply/persist
dropped.finding: `rebar.bridge_sync()` (and MCP `bridge_sync`) execute a mutating live pass via `orchestrator.run_pass_result(...)`, which calls `reconcile.reconcile_once` directly and never acquires the reconciler pass-lock, starts a heartbeat, checks the in-flight lock, or honors the durable pause — all of which `main()` performs before a normal live pass. A live sync can therefore run concurrently with another pass and while the bridge is paused.
